issues.detail: Pitfalls cover a few cases, but the code samples have no error handling for task failures, actor crashes, retries, or Serve deployment errors.
The two Examples entries are prose descriptions that point back to earlier snippets rather than self-contained realistic demonstrations with input and output.

scenarios.name: parallelize-slow-calls-with-ray-core
scenarios.rationale: Both decorate with @ray.remote, call ray.init(), put the table once with ray.put and pass the ref, and submit all tasks before a single ray.get; B is slightly cleaner and more precise (it states the top-level ObjectRef resolution caveat and shows a complete script with the 500 IDs), while A adds extra variants (actor pool, ray.wait loop) that go beyond the rubric but don't add rubric coverage.

scenarios.name: serve-sentiment-model-with-composition
scenarios.rationale: A matches the rubric on all three points: separate deployments composed with .bind(), awaited handle.method.remote calls, host and port set through serve.start(http_options) bound to 127.0.0.1, and no num_gpus. B composes the deployments correctly and has no GPU option, but it sets host and port with the `serve run` CLI flags instead of serve.start(http_options=...), and it calls handles without a method name. B also adds an unneeded num_cpus actor option.

scenarios.name: tune-learning-rate-with-asha
scenarios.rationale: Both responses meet every rubric item: tune.Tuner, loguniform and choice in param_space, ASHAScheduler, TuneConfig with metric, mode and num_samples=20, tune.report, tuner.fit(), and get_best_result with the config and loss printed. B is slightly cleaner, with a self-contained trainable and a note that tune.run is deprecated. A adds useful notes on minimum loss and tune.with_parameters, but its get_best_result call repeats the metric and mode already set in TuneConfig.
